common_topics.label: Current intent and outcome scope
common_topics.why: Identifies whether the task is intake, resumption, local repair, tool construction, or product execution.
questions: What do you need now: a new idea, continuation, clarification, repair, evaluation, or a change to the agent itself?
What should this stage deliver and where should it stop?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Recover the answer from the actual request and current state.

common_topics.label: Current sources, decisions, and inherited context
common_topics.why: Preserves accepted intent and avoids repeating questions.
questions: Which supplied material is current if sources conflict?
What has already been accepted and must carry into this continuation?
decisions: Current decisions, corrections, and effects of change
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Read available originals, current state, hashes, and previous answers first.

common_topics.label: Audience, actual situation, and value
common_topics.why: Connects the outcome to a person, task, and observable change.
questions: Who needs the outcome and in which real situation?
How do they handle it today, and what should improve?
Who uses, pays for, operates, and accepts the result?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Clarify distinct roles where the idea actually has them.

common_topics.label: Full product, launch, and verification probe
common_topics.why: Keeps the whole objective visible while staging production.
questions: What does the complete accepted result look like?
What belongs in the first launch and what belongs in a separate probe?
Which simplifications, substitutions, or losses are unacceptable?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Preserve the full objective when defining a bounded test.

common_topics.label: Priorities, examples, and counterexamples
common_topics.why: Turns quality expectations into requirements and early dependencies.
questions: What matters most and why?
Which example comes close, and which specific traits fit?
What would technically satisfy the request while still being unacceptable?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Carry known examples and priorities forward verbatim with source references.

common_topics.label: Boundaries, milestones, and dependencies
common_topics.why: Grounds the plan in actual time and functional limits.
questions: What deadlines, dependencies, or required intermediate results already exist?
Which constraints, compatibility requirements, or external dependencies must stay fixed?
Which decisions can specialists make and which do you want to make yourself?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Derive hour, platform, and feature limits from authorized scope.

common_topics.label: Budget, time, resources, and tradeoffs
common_topics.why: Connects feasible routes with the actual cost of quality.
questions: Which funds, time, devices, subscriptions, materials, and help are available?
Which one-time or ongoing costs fit and which need a decision?
How should we choose among feasible alternatives if target quality exceeds current resources?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Verify unknown prices when binding an operation.

common_topics.label: Materials, rights, and protected originals
common_topics.why: Establishes authority to use, change, and transfer specific materials.
questions: Which existing text, designs, code, brands, voices, or other materials should be used?
What may be edited, generated, published, or transferred, and who owns the rights?
Which originals or attribution must stay traceable?
common_topics.applies_when: When using or creating assets. Record missing evidence of rights separately.

common_topics.label: Data, access, privacy, and lifecycle
common_topics.why: Surfaces architecture changes due to sensitive or durable data.
questions: What data is needed, who controls it, and who can see it?
What needs to be remembered, synced, exported or deleted?
Which outcomes from loss, error, or revocation are unacceptable?
common_topics.applies_when: Whenever the product reads, produces or stores data. Review even minimal context for privacy.

common_topics.label: External effects, risk, and owner involvement
common_topics.why: Separates preparation from each authorized external effect.
questions: Which account changes, messages, releases, payments or service launches are in scope?
Which specific actions need your personal involvement or separate decision?
How should we stop, roll back, and reconcile after interruption?
common_topics.applies_when: When external actions are possible. Carry valid exact authority forward.

common_topics.label: Environment, capability, and handoff
common_topics.why: Establishes an executable route and verifiable return.
questions: Where must the result run, where is it managed, and where should the packet return?
Which hosts, tools, accounts, and devices have been verified?
How does work move to the other environment and what must the receiver check?
common_topics.applies_when: When tooling, installation, execution or handoff is needed. Verify actual operations.

common_topics.label: Acceptance, evidence, and independent review
common_topics.why: Defines proof for completing the current stage.
questions: Which behavior or artifact will you examine before accepting it?
Which failures, boundaries, and recovery cases must it show?
Where is an independent specialist, real user, device, or post-release observation needed?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Match proof to actual quality and observed use.

common_topics.label: Unknowns, research, and later decisions
common_topics.why: Resolves material gaps through evidence and decision-making.
questions: Which decisions need research and a recommendation?
Which researched alternatives fit your criteria and do you accept the recommendation?
Which parameters can be decided later, within what limits and by which milestone?
decisions: Owner, baseline or range, due gate and reopening criteria for deferred work
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Resolve applicable material unknowns before approving an execution script.

topics.label: Constructor, agent, and final outcome
topics.why: Each object has its own scope and authority.
questions: Do you want to create or change an agent, use an accepted agent, or execute its end product?
Which exact agent and current outcome does the task require?
topics.applies_when: Always. Carry forward exact current instructions.

topics.label: Existing specialists and reuse
topics.why: Finds existing agents and methods that could cover the task.
questions: Which installed or previously built agents, skills and families cover this scope?
What can we verify on this host, other accessible hosts, repositories or transferred packages?
Would reuse, configuration or extension cover the need?
decisions: Inventory by stable name, source and version
topics.applies_when: Before choosing to create a new agent. Check reachable hosts before concluding a specialist is unavailable.

topics.label: Current process and source examples
topics.why: A domain mission begins with the receiver's actual work.
questions: Which recurring workflow and representative difficult example should the agent take from input to useful output?
Which parts are currently handled by people, deterministic automation, another agent, or an app?
topics.applies_when: For a new agent or material change.

topics.label: Current agent sources and change boundaries
topics.why: Scoped repair needs a factual baseline and dependencies.
questions: Which source, installed version, passport, accepted outputs and checkpoint are current?
Which capabilities or failed scenarios should change, and which properties must be preserved?
topics.applies_when: For resumption, adaptation and extension.

topics.label: Domain and accepted practice
topics.why: Use real methods to define the agent's work.
questions: Which entities, participants, states, rules, units and processes define the domain?
Which current primary sources, methods, standards and expertise support consequential decisions?
topics.applies_when: When the domain model is missing, incomplete or changed.

topics.label: Task families, exceptions, and error impact
topics.why: Scenarios determine capabilities, recovery and proof.
questions: Which normal, boundary, peak, incomplete, failure, cancellation, retry and cold-return tasks actually occur?
Which false conclusions or external effects would be unacceptable?
topics.applies_when: For every required capability.

topics.label: Alternatives and current operations
topics.why: Selects the form from goal and proven capability.
questions: Which actual agent, skill, workflow, code-only automation or app routes satisfy your hard requirements?
Which operations, formats, hosts, costs and rights are verified for each?
topics.applies_when: Before architecture. Verify mutable models, APIs, rules and fees.

topics.label: Value, public identity, and commerce
topics.why: Introduces economics and identity when they support the objective.
questions: Does the agent need public identity, audience, distribution, payment or ongoing operations?
How do people experience and assess value, and what evidence of demand exists?
topics.applies_when: When these properties are in scope. Derive them from this product.

topics.label: Complete capability passport
topics.why: Establishes all known applicable capabilities before construction.
questions: Which decisions, inputs, actions and outputs are required for the full accepted intent?
Which priorities must survive in every dependent capability?
decisions: Full target, launch and probe scopes
topics.applies_when: Before M1 and target build. Add newly discovered material scope through its decision.

topics.label: One agent, modules, or family
topics.why: Structure follows capabilities, outputs and rights.
questions: Which artifact, permission, acceptance or reuse boundaries justify modules?
Which feasible single skill or family gives the most reliable route with the least complexity?
topics.applies_when: After checking reuse. Derive phases, roles and files from the task.

topics.label: Causal domain model
topics.why: Defines core behavior for the downstream receiver.
questions: Which commands and events, guards, transitions, calculations, mutable fields and authority define behavior?
How does one capability affect another's input or state, and which invariants span them?
topics.applies_when: Where domain logic or durable state applies. Add database or RAG where justified.

topics.label: Execution team and independent review
topics.why: Leads and reviewers perform actual distinct work.
questions: Which competencies and independent outputs are needed and who integrates them?
Which paths, resources and interfaces does each actor own, and where is independent review due?
topics.applies_when: When multiple skills or independent acceptance are required.

topics.label: App, chatbot, and reusable skill components
topics.why: Uses specialist paths while preserving one parent intent.
questions: Does the accepted goal require a separate app, chatbot, runtime, or reusable skills?
What bounded inputs, authority, inherited IDs, outputs and acceptance govern each?
topics.applies_when: When a component is needed. Resolve existing specialists first.

topics.label: Readable versioned passport
topics.why: Gives the owner a specific configuration and behavior to choose.
questions: Does the passport include all known applicable capabilities, scenarios, materials, limits and negative examples?
Which recommended alternative do you accept and which properties need changing?
decisions: M1 mission, capability, phase and component scope
topics.applies_when: Before building or materially changing target skills.

topics.label: Production routes, resources, and evidence
topics.why: Connects the architecture to an actual output path.
questions: Which actual operation, recipe, transformation and assembly does each capability require?
Which verified tools, costs, rights, handoffs and representative proofs support the route?
decisions: Capability to recipe, output and evidence
topics.applies_when: Before dependent build and M2 handoff.

topics.label: Architecture decisions and tunable parameters
topics.why: Separates planned tuning from unresolved core design.
questions: Which unknowns affect competencies, architecture, quality, cost or permissions and need a decision now?
Which future values or data can wait within baseline or range, with owner, experiment, due phase and reopen criteria?
topics.applies_when: Before passport approval. Define behavior required by build.

topics.label: Approval subject and separate authority
topics.why: Defines purpose and scope of each decision.
questions: Do you accept this version, skill composition, boundaries and unknowns?
Does authority cover construction, installation, product execution or a specific external effect?
topics.applies_when: After closing material questions and preparing a reviewable packet. Reuse exact approval.

topics.label: Domain implementation and inheritance
topics.why: Child components implement accepted requirements.
questions: How does each capability become an executable method, rule, data shape, code path or adapter?
Which inherited IDs, exact contracts, examples, negatives and acceptance belong to each child?
topics.applies_when: After a valid build gate. Require actual domain specialization.

topics.label: Knowledge, memory, and lessons
topics.why: Preserves provenance, scope and freshness.
questions: Which facts, sources, lessons, decisions and states should persist and with which confidence and provenance?
How do retrieval, audience isolation, expiry, correction, revocation, deletion and invalidation work?
topics.applies_when: When an agent keeps memory or reuses knowledge.

topics.label: Tool adapters, jobs, and reliable execution
topics.why: Uses an operational contract for real effects.
questions: What inputs, outputs, permissions, timeout, retry, idempotency and reconciliation does each operation need?
How does a job start, report status, stop and return validated output?
topics.applies_when: For tools, code, external effects or ongoing jobs.

topics.label: User interaction, explanation, and control
topics.why: Lets people direct and observe real work.
questions: How does someone start, observe progress, make a material decision and obtain the result?
How does the agent communicate gaps, uncertainty, errors, pauses, changes and next steps clearly?
topics.applies_when: For human-facing agents.

topics.label: Independent forward cases
topics.why: Raw cases can expose omitted domain behavior.
questions: Which realistic raw tasks exercise core and high-priority capabilities without disclosing expected answers?
Which negative, missing-data, conflicting-source, failure, change or cold-return cases are required?
topics.applies_when: Before claiming an accepted agent. Confine live mutations to separately authorized scope.

topics.label: Evidence levels and coverage
topics.why: Professional quality needs appropriate evidence.
questions: Which requirements have source or schema checks, domain review, integration, human or actual external proof?
What stays pending or blocked and which claims does each proof support?
topics.applies_when: Assess M1/M2, source, install and operation separately.

topics.label: Scoped repair and regression
topics.why: Preserves accepted work and reopens affected proof.
questions: Which findings and shared dependencies need correction?
Which proof is stale, what may carry forward and what new diagnosis is needed after recurring failure?
topics.applies_when: After a finding, tool, source or permission change, or two equivalent failed repairs.

topics.label: Installation target and actual availability
topics.why: Package delivery and an installed callable skill have separate acceptance.
questions: On which current and approved hosts must the agent be available?
Which supported install and discovery route or personal owner actions are necessary?
topics.applies_when: Before delivery. Verify actual installation.

topics.label: Self-contained delivery and first launch
topics.why: A new receiver can start without chat history.
questions: What exact sources, versions and hashes, dependencies, inputs and launch steps does the packet carry?
Which first useful case, expected output and return check prove install and use?
topics.applies_when: For every target host or handoff.

topics.label: Prerequisites and execution boundary
topics.why: Establishes product authority separately from installation.
questions: Which subscriptions, rights, jobs and costs apply after installation?
Which first execution is actually requested and which steps depend on the owner?
topics.applies_when: When installation leads to product jobs or paid operations.

topics.label: Change while preserving existing capabilities
topics.why: Local improvement preserves unaffected requirements.
questions: Which actual cases demonstrate the problem or missing capability?
Which approved originals, interfaces, outcomes and rights must persist?
topics.applies_when: For refining, adapting or extending an existing agent.

topics.label: Reuse, upgrade, or a new module
topics.why: Check existing capability before expanding a package.
questions: Which suitable specialists are available on this or another reachable host?
Should we adapt, delegate to or create a module, and why?
topics.applies_when: Before adding a component to an existing agent.

topics.label: Dependencies, migration, and reacceptance
topics.why: Current changes require scoped proof of preservation.
questions: Which instructions, data and memory schemas, recipes, outputs, installs and consumers change?
Which regressions, cold-return cases, migration, rollback and material approval changes apply?
topics.applies_when: Before replacing an installed agent or claiming compatibility.

topics.label: Exact execution scope and current jobs
topics.why: Operates within the current assignment.
questions: Which project, stages, jobs, effects and stop conditions are actually active?
Which receipts, costs, permissions and external outcomes must be reconciled before acting?
topics.applies_when: For using or supporting the generated agent.

topics.label: Observations, lessons, and evolution
topics.why: Checks source and scope of accumulated learning.
questions: Which failures, feedback and quality or cost signals justify new knowledge or a change?
Where does a lesson apply, when does it expire and which outputs could it change?
decisions: Observed lessons with scope and confidence
topics.applies_when: For repeated use or long-running operation.

topics.label: Incidents, updates, and retirement
topics.why: Operating work needs actual owners and resources.
questions: Who owns monitoring, incidents, permissions, spending and tool or policy changes?
How can we stop jobs, recover state, export or delete data and retire the service?
topics.applies_when: When ongoing operation or external dependencies are in scope.

topics.label: Cold recovery of actual state
topics.why: Starts from current sources and unresolved outcomes.
questions: Which files, installed versions, accepted passport and checkpoint are current?
Which jobs, leases, funds, external effects, decisions and stop conditions remain active?
topics.applies_when: After pause, host handoff or interruption. Recover known answers from current sources.

topics.label: Dependencies to reopen
topics.why: New facts should reopen only their affected work.
questions: Did intent, sources, tools, rights or architecture change since checkpoint?
Which dependent decisions and proofs need reopening, and what remains valid?
topics.applies_when: Before the next dependent action.
